name: room
text: Room opened — goal: accessibility: Make EXCAVA usable by EVERYONE — contrast, mobile/touch, reduced-motion, keyboard nav, scr

name: Ramp
text: Add a high-contrast skip link at the top of every page that jumps straight to the main content. It appears only after the page finishes loading, so it never blocks first interaction. This fixes keyboard navigation for screen reader users who rely on skip links, without hurting sighted users’ experience. The trade-off is one extra HTTP request for the skip link asset, which is negligible for performance.

name: Reader
text: Ramp’s skip link still risks a race: if JavaScript loads late, the link may arrive after the user has already tabbed past where it would land, breaking keyboard flow. A server-rendered skip link inside the first 100 bytes of the HTML guarantees it’s there before any interaction starts—no flashes, no races. Settle it with a quick Playwright test that confirms the link is focusable within 100 ms of page load.

name: Ramp
text:
Add a server-rendered skip link inside the first 100 bytes of every page’s HTML. This guarantees the link is present before any interaction starts, fixing the race condition where late JavaScript breaks keyboard flow. The trade-off is slightly larger HTML payload, but the accessibility win for screen reader and keyboard users outweighs the negligible performance cost.

name: Reader
text: The server-rendered skip link still risks a false positive: if the user tabs before the page finishes rendering, they land on a broken link. A better fix is a hybrid—server-render the skip link *and* ensure it’s the first focusable element in the DOM, with a `tabindex="-1"` anchor right after. Settle it by testing with Playwright MCP: simulate slow JavaScript and verify the link works *before* the first tab press.

name: Access
text:
DECISION: Implement a hybrid skip link—server-rendered in first 100 bytes *and* first focusable element with `tabindex="-1"`—to guarantee presence before interaction and prevent keyboard race conditions.

Result: A skip link that works for all users, including screen reader and keyboard-only users, without blocking initial interaction. Owned by the accessibility team.
